correctness.rationale: The barycentric orbit triangulation is exact. For each free vertex orbit, eligible internal edge orbits are precisely perfect matchings indexed by involutions; between distinct vertex orbits every edge orbit is a perfect matching. If chosen inter-orbit matchings contain a quotient cycle its finite lift contains a cycle; if not, the lift is k disjoint tree copies per component. One internal matching joins distinct copies without cycling; two add k edges to k components and force a cycle. These are exactly forests of Q. Graphic-matroid shellability gives integral sphere wedges, and an exponential set-partition count of signed forests gives the closed coefficient formula. All edge cases m=1 and s=0 are treated explicitly. 104557 lifted-vs-model selections and independent weighted Tutte computations agree, but are only corroboration.

originality.rationale: The new implication identifies geometric fixed points of the graphic-matroid forest complex under every freely acting finite group with a specific multigraph matroid whose apex multiplicity equals the number of involutions. The inspected primary literature proves ordinary matroid shellability, Tutte enumerations, gain-graph cycle theory and biconed-forest formulas without asserting this orbit-fixed identification. Closest indexed findings address different complexes or ordinary automorphism homology. The explicit cycle-lifting and internal-orbit argument is not furnished by those comparisons, but older voltage-graph literature remains a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: Older voltage/regular-cover or equivariant graphic-matroid literature may contain an equivalent orbit-face identification not indexed by title and abstract.

value.rationale: For every finite group and every number of free vertex orbits, a natural and large geometric fixed-space complex reduces to a small explicit graphic-matroid forest complex with parameters (m, group order, number of involutions). This gives a complete integral homotopy classification and exact computable Betti number, including a sharp dimension jump depending on involution existence, motivating the exact calculation independently of any downstream theorem. It is neither a parameter substitution into a prior fixed-point result nor merely a finite census.
